plotSections.title: Beacon bet and the return from Trigash
bullets: Haldor sets aside a portal opened in Carlkin's house and his pursuit of a cutpurse because the day is now about the spirit problem.

Gerk recaps the day: they spoke with Carlkin, he practiced doorway magic in a safe place away from people, and Sylan practiced with the hoard lantern-staff. Sylan blinded Gerk, spirits went into Sylan, those spirits wanted to go home, and Sylan can send them — including bad spirits still in town. Haldor places this in Trigash Forest around mid-morning.

Erwin won 25 gold from Haldor. Erwin saw the beacon and the group fly that way with a dragon; Haldor had bet it was a random event rather than the stronghold hooligans. About an hour later the flyers came back out of the forest and reached town roughly 45 minutes before this talk. Gerk says he walked. The forest is a couple of miles out.

plotSections.title: City bans
bullets: Spirit-sucking is against New Navel's rules. Haldor hoped Gerk had the interdimensional shackles; Gerk does not, and he will not open a door to fetch them.

Haldor reads a notice from a vest notepad: extradimensional and interdimensional doors are now prohibited inside the city limits. He tells Gerk to practice that magic in the forest. Spirit-sucking is prohibited as well.
Gerk walks Haldor straight to Sylan and says he will tell him to stop.

plotSections.title: The six spirits and Ledzbika
bullets: Haldor greets Sylan as under the weather from sucking up spirits and mentions a spirit jar.

Sylan says he is a cleric and servant of the Raven Queen, tasked with finding people who escaped their end. He thinks he accidentally took six people from New Navel while Ord used the lantern. The lantern let Ord see the spirits following Sylan; Sylan says the party could already see spirits, and he sent these on because that was his duty. He remembers an older humanoid woman most clearly and did not keep their names.

Haldor has had no recent missing persons. Ord remembers a hostile man who disliked them and wanted to give something back to Sylan, and a frightened woman who wanted help and did not want to go back. When the spirits were struck they became tangible and started changing.

One was an elderly high-elf man, Ledzbika, who named his neighbor Claire Belle. Haldor remembers Ledzbika's rants that the neighbor was trying to steal his things. Ledzbika died about a month ago of natural causes and did not come back as an echo, which Haldor calls the head-scratcher. A half-remembered name, Hofford, does not stick.

plotSections.title: Echoes versus undead
bullets: Haldor says he knows nothing about gods. New Navel's returned dead are echoes, celestial forms of themselves, not ghosts. Undead are undead, and spirits fall under undead. A portal into another dimension indicates these were not corporeal. Summoning undead is against town rules, so the lantern stays under wraps or he will confiscate it. Sylan agrees.
Sylan fears either that he has failed his duty to find lost souls, or that New Navel traps souls.

Haldor says the echoes were residents or travelers of the town when it was Neville. They escaped a prison of sorts without realizing it, died, and could choose a normal death or return as a celestial echo of themselves. He guesses an elder god tied to the sea. He credits that choice with the city not being full of undead.
Besides Ledzbika, Haldor estimates a handful, give or take a dozen, deaths in the last six or seven months, plus travelers. He calls New Navel a frontier town on a rough road.

chronologicalEvents: 1. Haldor drops the Carlkin house portal and the cutpurse to deal with the spirit problem.

2. Gerk recaps Carlkin, safe doorway practice, the lantern-staff, Gerk being blinded, spirits entering Sylan, and spirits who want to be sent home, including bad spirits in town. Haldor sets this in Trigash Forest, mid-morning.

3. Haldor admits he owes Erwin 25 gold. Erwin was right that the beacon was the stronghold group flying toward the forest with a dragon; they flew back about an hour later. Gerk walked. Town is a couple of miles from the forest, and the flyers arrived about 45 minutes ago.
4. Haldor and Gerk go to find Sylan. Spirit-sucking is illegal. Gerk does not have interdimensional shackles and will not open a city door to get them.
5. Haldor reads a new city notice: extradimensional and interdimensional doors are prohibited inside the city. Practice belongs in the forest, and spirit-sucking is also banned.
6. Gerk leads Haldor to Sylan. Haldor shakes his hand and says he sounds under the weather from sucking up spirits.

7. Sylan explains the Raven Queen duty, the accidental taking of about six New Navel people, and Ord seeing them with the lantern so they could be sent on. He offers the older woman as the clearest memory.
8. Haldor has no new missing persons. Ord describes the hostile man, the frightened woman who did not want to go back, and spirits turning tangible and changing when struck.
9. They name Ledzbika, the elderly high-elf man who accused neighbor Claire Belle. Haldor says Ledzbika died about a month ago of natural causes and did not return as an echo.

10. Haldor separates celestial echoes from undead spirits, forbids summoning undead, and orders the lantern kept hidden or confiscated. Sylan complies and raises the lost-souls duty versus a soul trap.
11. Haldor explains old Neville as a prison the dead escaped without knowing, and the choice to return as a celestial echo, possibly from a sea-related elder god.
12. Recent deaths besides Ledzbika are a handful to about a dozen over six or seven months, plus travelers, in what Haldor calls a frontier town.

Haldor.existing: Sheriff of New Navel who bans doors and spirit-taking inside the city.
notes: He will not investigate the portal opened in Carlkin's house and was going back to catching a cutpurse before the spirit matter took the day.
He bet Erwin 25 gold that the Trigash beacon was a random event. Erwin won: the stronghold group flew that way with a dragon and returned about an hour later.
Spirit-sucking is illegal. He hoped Gerk had interdimensional shackles for the problem.
He reads a notice that extradimensional and interdimensional doors are now prohibited within the city limits and tells Gerk to practice in the forest.
He has no recent missing persons. He remembers Ledzbika as an elderly man who died about a month ago of natural causes and often ranted that his neighbor was stealing his things.
He says town echoes are celestials, not ghosts, while spirits are undead, and that summoning undead is forbidden. He will confiscate the lantern if it is not kept under wraps.
He describes the town's older name, Neville, as a prison of sorts the dead escaped without realizing, with a choice to return as a celestial echo, possibly tied to a sea-related elder god.
Over the last six or seven months he estimates a handful, give or take a dozen, local deaths plus travelers, and he calls New Navel a frontier town.
personality: He is rule-first, dismissive of gods, and willing to leave forest practice alone if the city bans are kept.
quotesThemes: Extradimensional and interdimensional doors are prohibited within the city limits, and spirit-sucking is not permitted.
They are echoes, not ghosts: echoes are celestials, and spirits fall under undead.
Summoning undead is against the rules, and the lantern stays under wraps or he will confiscate it.
Ledzbika not returning as an echo is the head-scratcher.

Erwin.existing: New Navel man who won 25 gold betting the Trigash beacon was the stronghold hooligans.
notes: He saw the giant beacon, bet Haldor 25 gold that it was the stronghold hooligans rather than a random event, and won.
He saw them fly toward the forest with a dragon, and they came back out about an hour later.

Gerk.existing: Half-orc barbarian and Doorman who opens arch doorways.
notes: He practiced interdimensional doors in a safe place away from people after they spoke with Carlkin, and he was blinded while Sylan used the lantern-staff.
He does not have the interdimensional shackles. He suggests opening a door to them would go poorly, and he accepts the city ban.
He walked back from the forest while others flew, then led Haldor straight to Sylan and agreed to tell him to stop sucking spirits.
He reports that the spirits wanted to go home, that Sylan can send them, and that bad spirits in town still need to be sent home.

Sylan.existing: Half-elf rogue and Gilbrick Gatekeeper with a cautious bond to the Raven Queen.
notes: He tells Haldor he is a cleric and servant of the Raven Queen, tasked with finding people who escaped their end.
He believes he accidentally took six New Navel people. He did not keep their names. The older humanoid woman is the one he remembers most, and he had the closest interaction with her.
He says Ord's lantern showed the spirits following him so they could be sent on, which he treated as his duty.
He identifies Ledzbika and passes on that Ledzbika's neighbor was Claire Belle. A possible spirit name, Hofford, is only half-remembered.
He agrees to keep the lantern under wraps. He is worried he has failed his duty, or that New Navel traps souls.
personality: He frames the spirit-taking as duty, then immediately worries it was a mistake.
quotesThemes: He is a cleric of the Raven Queen, tasked with finding people who have escaped their end.
openQuestions: Who were the other spirits, especially the older woman he remembers most?
Has he failed to find people who escaped their end, or does New Navel trap souls?

Ord.existing: Dragonborn paladin and Gatekeeper of Feldspar.
notes: He was working the lantern in Trigash Forest. Sylan says that let Ord see the spirits following Sylan.
He remembers the first spirit as hostile and wanting to give something back to Sylan, and the woman as scared, wanting help, and unwilling to go back.
He remembers the spirits becoming tangible and changing when they were hit.
He recognizes the elderly high-elf man as Ledzbika.

Ledzbika.existing: Elderly half-elf spirit pulled from rest, trying to return to his abode.
notes: Sylan and Ord identify him among the spirits taken in the forest: an elderly high-elf man.
He told them his neighbor was Claire Belle, matching the rants Haldor remembers about a neighbor trying to steal his things.
Haldor says he died about a month ago of natural causes and did not return as one of the town's celestial echoes. Haldor calls that the head-scratcher.
A fleeting extra name, Hofford, was suggested and then dropped.
personality: Haldor remembers him by his frequent rants.
openQuestions: Why did Ledzbika come back as a spirit instead of a celestial echo?

Carlkin.existing: Turtle-like person whose lighthouse in New Navel is his home and bookshop.
notes: The party spoke with him before the woods.
Haldor knows a portal was opened in Carlkin's house and chooses not to investigate it. Carlkin goes back to his own devices.

Fused lantern-staff.existing: Fused lantern and staff that reveals the Ethereal Plane and draws nearby spirits when held active.
notes: Sylan had them practice with the hoard staff in Trigash Forest. Using it blinded Gerk, and spirits then went into Sylan.
Sylan says Ord's use of the lantern let Ord see the spirits following Sylan, even though the party could already see spirits.
Haldor treats it as a magic item that reveals spirits and connects it to summoning undead. It must be kept under wraps in town or he will confiscate it.

Interdimensional shackles.existing: Restraints Haldor hoped to use on the spirit problem, which Gerk does not have.
notes: Haldor asks again while going to confront Sylan. Gerk confirms he does not have them.
Gerk floats opening a door to the shackles and agrees that would go poorly, especially under the city door ban.

New Navel.existing: Familiar stop that sends trade caravans to the party's tavern in Langdale and holds Carlkin's lighthouse.
notes: Extradimensional and interdimensional doors are now prohibited inside the city limits. Spirit-sucking and summoning undead are also forbidden. Haldor points magic practice to Trigash Forest.
Haldor reports no recent missing persons.

When the town was Neville, residents and travelers later described it as a prison they escaped without realizing. The dead could choose a normal death or return as celestial echoes, which Haldor ties loosely to a sea-related elder god and credits with the lack of rampant undead.
Besides Ledzbika, about a handful to a dozen people died in the last six or seven months, plus an unknown number of travelers. Haldor calls it a frontier town on a rough road.
quotesThemes: Echoes are celestials; spirits are undead.

Trigash Forest.existing: Forest outskirts where a beacon was raised and spirits stayed back.
notes: Haldor identifies it as the place of the beacon, the blinding, and the spirits entering Sylan, around mid-morning.
It is a couple of miles from town, a decent walk of well under an hour by air.
Haldor tells Gerk to do his prohibited city magic out there.

Celestial echo.existing: New Navel's dead who return as celestial forms of themselves, not ghosts or undead.
notes: Haldor repeats that echoes are celestials and are different from undead spirits.
They were residents or travelers who died after escaping Neville and chose to come back as celestial forms of their prior selves instead of dying normally.
He guesses the choice has to do with an elder god connected to the sea, and he says this is why the city is not full of undead.
Ledzbika, dead about a month, did not become an echo, which Haldor cannot explain.
quotesThemes: When they died they had a choice: die normally, or come back as a celestial echo of themselves.
openQuestions: Why did Ledzbika not return as a celestial echo?
